results.summary_before: This design drives a 7-segment display so that entering the value 201 in binary on the inputs lights the segments to form the letter A. The pin names are simply the fixed logic values 1 and 0 for each input and output, reflecting a hard-wired pattern rather than a general decoder. It is tested by running the design and adjusting the inputs if needed. No external hardware is required, and the project is a first Wokwi exercise by the author.

results.summary_before: This is a guitar tuner design that measures the frequency of input pulses and displays the result on a 7-segment display. It uses a fixed window approach for frequency discrimination, dividing the clock and converting binary to decimal for display. The design requires external hardware to condition the analog input signal into clean digital pulses, as detailed in the Neptune project. It is notable for being part of the Neptune tuner series and includes a slower square wave output on one pin.

results.notes: Summary is supported, but the term 'FP16' in the pin names is treated as the input format, not strict IEEE FP16.
results.summary_before: This design implements a multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit for 16-bit DLFloat (a custom floating-point format). It accepts two sets of eight FP16 inputs via the ui and uio pins and outputs a 16-bit result in two 8-bit halves over two clock cycles. An external FPGA is required to drive the inputs and capture the output, as the data is presented in a multiplexed manner. A silicon test report confirms functionality, noting a timing discrepancy in the provided cocotb test that was resolved.
